title: Vocalion recordings in London with Leonard Feather
summary: Feather set up and produced all his London recordings, and the playing ban stayed because of exchange restrictions.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Right. Then you -- at the end of these tours, you always went back to London and you made a number of recording sessions there with Vocalion I think, a new label, and Leonard Feather, I think, was involved in some of those.
Well, I think Leonard was involved in all of them.
Yes, he set them up, and he, I guess, was what you would call the producer.
Right. Did you try at that time to get them to relax the restriction against playing? Or did you sort of give that up after you saw the lay of the land?

Well, I guess I didn't work at it very hard. I think Leonard was always trying to do something about it, you know, and other people there, but they were pretty adamant because of the situation that existed with English musicians coming in to America -- and of course, they were quite justified, I felt, and still feel that way.
